messages:
laura: Manager question  they're asking to push a mid-cycle merit outside the normal window due to an unexpected scope increase. Is this treated as an out-of-cycle comp-change or a spot bonus? what's simpler operationally?
omar: Operationally a spot bonus is faster (one-time cash) but affects tax/payroll differently. If manager wants a base increase (permanent) use the comp-change form. Spot bonus form: https://redwood-internal/forms/spot-bonus. comp-change: https://redwood-internal/forms/comp-change
ben: Finance note: spot bonuses draw from Bonus budget buckets and usually require Manager + Finance lead signoff. Permanent comp increases need full comp-change routing, run-rate calc, and People Ops signoff. Run-rate impacts headcount budget vs one-time bonus which hits current period.
anya: Manager asked if we can do "hybrid" (small base bump + small spot) to split impact. allowed?
kevin: Yes, hybrid is allowed but submit two items: comp-change for the base bump and spot-bonus request for the one-time. That makes auditing clearer. Also include a short memo explaining why split was chosen.
laura: If we go permanent, what's the minimum evidence People Ops expects? manager prefers a short packet.
omar: Minimal packet: 1) 3-4 bullet evidence (scope + examples + impact) 2) run-rate calc table (current -> new -> delta) 3) cost center/GL 4) HRIS id 5) desired change date. Optional: peer notes or customer feedback.
ben: Also include whether the funding comes from headcount or discretionary budget. if it uses a hiring freeze exception, note that too.
anya: Timeline Q: can a comp-change submitted today land in next payroll (10 days out)?
kevin: If comp-change + all approvals + cost code are complete >= 6 business days before payroll close there's good chance. For spot bonuses the payroll lead needs the form >= 4 business days. If timeline is tight, mark the request [EXPEDITE] and DM @finance-lead + @people-ops-queue. No guarantees.
laura: Retro pay policy? manager wants base effective date back-dated by 4 weeks.
ben: Retro backdating for base increases is allowed but constrained. Finance prefers retro <= 60 days and will only process backpay for documented performance changes. Backpay > 60 days escalates to CFO. For spot bonuses retro doesn't apply (bonus paid in next run after approval).
anya: Any nuance for international employees? manager is in APAC and wants to do local currency.
omar: For international, include local payroll code, local tax treatment note, and confirm with Global Payroll. People Ops routes to Global Payroll automatically but DM them if urgent. Exchange rates will be applied at payroll run by Finance.
kevin: One more caveat: if the increase pushes an employee above market band mid-cycle, People Ops may request a comp committee review. That can add ~7-10 business days. Include market comp rationale if you anticipate band crossing.
laura: Audit prep: any quick checklist I can give the manager to avoid rework?
people-ops-bot: Automated minimal audit checklist: 1) Evidence bullets (3-4) 2) Run-rate calc present 3) HRIS employee ID 4) Cost center/GL attached 5) Mark [EXPEDITE] if time-sensitive and DM @people-ops-queue 6) For retro include exact effective date and justification 7) For international include local payroll code. See playbook: https://redwood-internal/playbooks/comp-change-audit
anya: Great. Manager also asked about combining equity with the comp packet to avoid two approvals.
ben: Equity cannot be combined in the comp-change intake. Equity flows through comp-ops and typically requires comp committee windows. You can submit both concurrently but expect separate review timelines.
laura: Perfect. i'll send this checklist to the manager and offer to review packet before submission. thanks everyone.
kevin: If you want, i'll run a quick budget sanity check once you have the run-rate numbers. DM me the calc.
people-ops-bot: Thread saved to People Ops playbook notes. Reply here if follow-ups needed.
